sources.title: S. C. Sahu, N. K. Dhal and R. C. Mohanty (2012), Tree species diversity, distribution and population structure in a tropical dry deciduous forest of Malyagiri hill ranges, Eastern Ghats, India
sources.publication: Tropical Ecology 53(2):163–168, 2012; International Society for Tropical Ecology
sources.method: Direct web open of author-deposited full original text on ResearchGate; page explicitly credits upload by SUDAM C. Sahu on 17 October 2017. Not a third-party summary. Downloaded PDF/visual page inspection unavailable in this pass.
sources.locator: Printed p.163 abstract; p.164 study-area and vegetation-analysis paragraphs. Relevant web text lines92–132,254–306.
sources.excerpt: Vegetation analysis was carried out during March 2007 to December 2009
claims: Eastern Ghats hill range in Pallahara subdivision, Angul.
Terrain consists of undulating hills and intervening valleys; p164 distinguishes lateritic hilltops and red clay/clay-loam valley soils.
60 tree plots, each20×20m, totaling2.4ha; 1063 trees from57 species; tree inclusion threshold at least15cm girth at breast height.
Sal (Shorea robusta) had highest importance-value index,44.67, in the sampled forest.
limits: 57 is sampled richness, not total species of the range or a current count.
Dominance belongs to the surveyed tropical dry deciduous forest, not every part of the range.
Do not treat cited medicinal uses as efficacy or dated pressure descriptions as fresh measurements.
No DOI verified; do not invent one.
Publisher PDF recovery and author PDF click failed; author-text reading is the actual method.
